declaration.intent: Define how any contributor or AI tool must write and edit repo-level meta-documentation (README.md, ROADMAP.md, CHANGELOG.md) for the Forge Stack. This is an operational instruction capsule — hand it directly to an editing assistant (e.g. Gemini in VS Code) alongside the current README.md and ROADMAP.md so edits stay consistent with the rest of the repo rather than drifting into generic AI-README style.

authority_order: Where this capsule conflicts with docs/glossary.md or a governance capsule, the glossary/governance wins — this capsule describes presentation, not the underlying terminology.
Where this capsule conflicts with CHANGELOG.md's recorded history, the changelog wins — never rewrite past entries to make current prose look better; add a new entry instead.

This capsule does not override giblets-forge/style/readme-style-v1, which governs James's personal README conventions across all his repos. This capsule is the Forge-Stack-specific layer on top of that.
hard_terminology_rules: SCP = protocol, sc = artefact, lowercase, .sc.json, never '.scp.json'. 'Capsule' is prose-only, never in code/schema/filenames.
DataCube = system (camel case), cube = artefact, lowercase.
Leighton Weight = the trust score (λ) an entity holds. Leighton Weight Engine = the stage/system. Never call the decay constant λ — it is always k.
ChronoSCRIBE is never shortened or abbreviated in documentation. 'ChronoScribe' (mixed case) is wrong.
HAL = Human Accountability Layer. Never expand or reinterpret the acronym.
British English throughout, including in code identifiers: authorise not authorize, artefact not artifact, -ise not -ize, with no exceptions for generated prose.
'sovereign AI stack', not 'AI framework', 'AI platform', or 'AI system' — the project's own self-description is fixed and should not be rephrased for variety.

additional_rules: The Status table's stage list, order, and artefact names must match the five-stage spine exactly as defined in the glossary: Declare/SCP/sc, Classify/DataCube/cube, Trust-score/Leighton Weight Engine/λ, Audit/ChronoSCRIBE/ledger, Act/HAL/seal. Never reorder, rename, or merge these rows.

Any claim that a stage is 'implemented' must be true at time of edit — check CHANGELOG.md's most recent relevant entries before asserting status, don't assume a stage stays implemented because an earlier entry said so.

Known Limitations must be reconciled against the actual current state of the code before every edit — a limitation that's been closed (e.g. by a later changelog entry) must be removed, not left stale; a new limitation surfaced by later work must be added, not omitted for tidiness.

Verification commands shown in the README must be runnable as literally written against the current tooling — if a flag, script name, or command has changed, the README example changes with it in the same edit.

roadmap_conventions.purpose: ROADMAP.md states what is not yet built and what is intentionally deferred — it is the forward-looking complement to CHANGELOG.md's backward-looking record. The two must never contradict each other.
structure: Group by spine stage or governance area, not by date — a roadmap organised by calendar date reads as a promise of when, which this project does not make.
Each item states: what is missing, why it matters, and what currently blocks it (a decision, a second person, real usage data, etc.) — not just a checkbox.

Distinguish explicitly between 'a decision not yet made' (governance work, cheap, no dependency) and 'a capability not yet buildable' (needs a second operator, needs real calibration data, etc.) — these are different kinds of blocked and must not be conflated into one undifferentiated backlog.
Never state a completion date or version number as a commitment. 'Next' or 'not yet started' are the only permitted urgency markers.

When an item is completed, it moves to CHANGELOG.md and is removed from ROADMAP.md in the same pass — a roadmap listing already-shipped work is stale and must be treated as a defect, not left as evidence of progress.
known_current_items: Cube file extension (.cube.json proposed, not ratified)
Whether the stack ships reference implementations per stage or protocol-only (the question AXIOM's scoping already answered once, unresolved elsewhere)
Capsule filename separator convention (hyphen vs underscore, inconsistent in the current set)
DataCube integrity denominator — governance ratification pending
Leighton k calibration — currently demonstration constants, no per-domain values ratified
Observation ingestion beyond v1-minimal explicit records
Outcome-to-λ-delta mapping — currently hardcoded, not ratified policy
HAL multi-validator flow and Tier 5 quorum — blocked on having more than one operator, not on more code

tone_and_scope_guardrails: An editing assistant working on README.md or ROADMAP.md must not invent new terminology, rename existing concepts for readability, or add marketing language not already present in the project's own docs.

If asked to make something 'sound more finished' or 'more impressive', the correct response is to improve clarity and structure, not to overstate status — see readme-style-v1's explicitly_forbidden list, which applies here without exception.
Any new claim about what the stack does must be checkable against an actual file in the repo (a capsule, the ledger, a doc) — if it can't be pointed at something real, it doesn't go in.
